newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 4.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Delta Air Lines is in talks about a possible acquisition of Continental Airlines.
- Three former Archer Daniels Midland Co officials were indicted by a federal grand jury on criminal antitrust charges.
- The Dow Jones industrials fell 79 points after a late-day sell-off.
- Miami will get an oversight board appointed by Florida's governor to help it grapple with its financial crisis.
- General Motors posted a 12 percent drop in November light-vehicle sales.
- New Home sales fell 8.7 percent in October.
- The FCC is preparing to grant MCI a valuable direct-broadcast license.
- Wall Street analysts could face regulatory heat if they disclose to clients more information than they publish in research reports and can't back it up.
- Microsoft set up a new decision-making group and shifted responsibilities to two rising stars.
- A.C. Nielsen agreed to stop certain business practices that were being investigated in the U.S. and Europe for possibly being anticompetitive.
- The Securities and Exchange Commission has put out word that it plans to give issuers of variable annuities a great deal of scrutiny.
- Boeing agred to hire McDonnell Douglas to help design and assemble larger commercial jets.
- Bond prices were almost unchanged after a partial retreat by the dollar erased earlier gains of as much as 5/8 point.
